en: The Path of Discrimination 1,
Great Chapter 1.4.
Discussion on the Faculties (Indriya-kathā)
1.4.1 First Exposition of the Discourse Thus have I heard:
at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus.
“Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
"Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. Which five?
“The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration,
and the faculty of wisdom— these, monks, are the five faculties.
In how many ways are these five faculties purified?
These five faculties are purified in fifteen ways.
By avoiding persons lacking faith, by serving, associating with, and attending upon persons endowed with faith, and by reflecting upon discourses that inspire confidence—
in these three ways, the faculty of faith is purified.
By avoiding persons who are indolent, by serving, associating with, and attending upon persons who have aroused energy, and by reviewing the right exertions—
in these three ways the faculty of energy is purified.
By avoiding persons who are muddle-minded, by serving, associating with, and attending upon persons whose mindfulness is established, and by reviewing the foundations of mindfulness—
The faculty of mindfulness is purified by these three ways:
by avoiding persons who are unconcentrated, by associating with, befriending, and attending upon persons who are concentrated, and by reviewing the meditative absorptions and liberations—
by these three ways the faculty of concentration is purified.
By avoiding persons of weak wisdom, by serving, associating with, and attending upon persons possessed of wisdom, and by reflecting upon the conduct of profound knowledge—
in these three ways the faculty of wisdom is purified.
Thus, by avoiding these five types of persons, by serving, associating with, and attending upon these five types of persons, and by reflecting upon these five aggregates of discourses—
By these fifteen aspects, these five faculties are purified.
In how many aspects are the five faculties developed? In how many aspects does the development of the five faculties occur?
In ten aspects the five faculties are developed; in ten aspects the development of the five faculties occurs.
Abandoning lack of faith, one develops the faculty of faith; developing the faculty of faith, one abandons lack of faith.
Abandoning laziness, one develops the faculty of energy; developing the faculty of energy, one abandons laziness.
Abandoning negligence, one develops the faculty of mindfulness; developing the faculty of mindfulness, one abandons negligence.
Abandoning restlessness, one develops the faculty of concentration; developing the faculty of concentration, one abandons restlessness.
Abandoning ignorance, one develops the faculty of wisdom; developing the faculty of wisdom, one abandons ignorance.
In these ten ways the five faculties are developed; in these ten ways there is the development of the five faculties.
In how many ways are the five faculties developed, well-developed?
In ten ways the five faculties are developed, well-developed.
Through the abandoning, the thorough abandoning of lack of faith, the faculty of faith is developed, well-developed.
Through the development and thorough development of the faculty of faith, lack of faith is abandoned and thoroughly abandoned.
Through the abandoning and thorough abandoning of laziness, the faculty of energy is developed and thoroughly developed;
through the development and thorough development of the faculty of energy, laziness is abandoned and thoroughly abandoned.
Because negligence has been abandoned and thoroughly abandoned, the faculty of mindfulness is developed and well-developed;
because the faculty of mindfulness has been developed and well-developed, negligence is abandoned and thoroughly abandoned.
Because restlessness has been abandoned and thoroughly abandoned, the faculty of concentration is developed and well-developed.
Through the development and thorough cultivation of the faculty of concentration, restlessness is abandoned and well-abandoned.
Through the abandoning of ignorance, the faculty of wisdom is developed and thoroughly cultivated;
through the development and thorough cultivation of the faculty of wisdom, ignorance is abandoned and well-abandoned.
In these ten ways, the five faculties are developed and well-developed.
In how many ways are the five faculties developed? In how many ways are the five faculties developed, well-developed, stilled, and thoroughly stilled?
In four ways are the five faculties developed; in four ways are the five faculties developed, well-developed, stilled, and thoroughly stilled.
At the moment of the path of stream-entry, the five faculties are being developed;

at the moment of the fruit of stream-entry, the five faculties have been developed and are well-developed, calmed and well-calmed. At the moment of the path of once-returning, the five faculties are being developed; [at the moment of the fruit of once-returning, the five faculties have been developed and are well-developed, calmed and well-calmed].
At the moment of the fruit of once-returning, the five faculties are both developed and well-developed, and both tranquilized and thoroughly tranquilized.
At the moment of the path of non-returning, the five faculties are being developed;
at the moment of the fruit of non-returning, the five faculties are both developed and well-developed, and both tranquilized and thoroughly tranquilized.
At the moment of the path of arahantship, the five faculties are being developed;
at the moment of the fruit of arahantship, the five faculties have been developed, are well-developed, are stilled, and are thoroughly stilled.
Thus there are four purifications of the paths, four purifications of the fruits, four purifications by eradication, and four purifications by subsiding.
In these four ways the five faculties are developed;
in these four ways the five faculties are developed, well-developed, calmed, and well-calmed.
For how many types of persons is there the development of the faculties?
How many persons have developed their faculties?
There is the development of the faculties for eight types of persons;
three types of persons are those who have developed their faculties.
Of which eight persons is there the cultivation of the faculties?
Of the seven types of trainees and of the virtuous worldling—
it is of these eight persons that there is the cultivation of the faculties.
Which three persons have developed faculties?

A disciple of the Tathāgata who has heard [the teaching] and whose taints are destroyed has developed faculties; a Paccekasambuddha who has awakened by himself to the true state of things has developed faculties; and a Tathāgata, an Arhat, a Perfectly Enlightened One, who is immeasurable, has developed faculties.
These are the three persons who have developed faculties.
Thus is the development of the faculties for these eight types of persons;
these three persons are those whose faculties are developed.
This is the first exposition of the discourses.
1.4.2. Second Exposition of the Discourse.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
“Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties.”
Which five?
The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom.
For whatever ascetics or brahmins, bhikkhus, [there may be] regarding the arising of these five faculties...
“Bhikkhus, those who do not understand as they really are the passing away, the gratification, the danger,
and the escape regarding these things are neither ascetics among ascetics nor brahmins among brahmins. Furthermore, these venerable ones do not,
by realizing it for themselves with direct knowledge, enter and dwell in the goal of the ascetic life or the goal of the brahmin life in this very world.”
But those recluses or brahmins, monks, who understand as they really are the origin, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape regarding these five faculties—
they, monks, among recluses are accounted true recluses, and among brahmins are accounted true brahmins.
"And those venerable ones, having realized for themselves through direct knowledge in this very life the goal of the ascetic life and the goal of the holy life, enter upon and abide in them.
In how many ways does the arising of the five faculties occur?
In how many ways does one understand the arising of the five faculties?
In how many ways does there come to be the subsiding of the five faculties?
In how many ways does one understand the subsiding of the five faculties?
In how many ways is there gratification in the five faculties? In how many ways does one understand the gratification in the five faculties?
In how many ways is there danger in the five faculties?
In how many ways does one understand the danger in the five faculties?
In how many ways is there escape from the five faculties?
In how many aspects does one understand the escape from the five faculties?
There are forty aspects in which the arising of the five faculties occurs;
in forty aspects one understands the arising of the five faculties.
The subsiding of the five faculties occurs in forty ways;
one understands the subsiding of the five faculties in forty ways.
The gratification of the five faculties occurs in twenty-five ways.
In twenty-five ways, one understands the gratification of the five faculties.
In twenty-five ways, there is danger in the five faculties;
in twenty-five ways, one understands the danger in the five faculties.
There is an escape from the five faculties by way of eighty modes; one understands the escape from the five faculties by way of eighty modes.
By which forty modes is there the arising of the five faculties?
In what forty ways does one understand the arising of the five faculties?
The arising of advertence for the purpose of resolution is the arising of the faith faculty;
through resolution, the arising of desire is the arising of the faith faculty; through resolution, the arising of attention...
The arising of faith-faculty is the arising of the faith-faculty; the establishment of unity by means of the faith-faculty is the arising of the faith-faculty.
The arising of adverting for the purpose of exertion is the arising of the energy-faculty; the arising of desire by means of exertion is the arising of the energy-faculty;
the arising of attention by means of exertion is the arising of the energy-faculty.
There is an arising: through the power of the faculty of energy, the establishment of unity is the arising of the faculty of energy;
through the advertence for the purpose of establishing, there is the arising of the faculty of mindfulness;
through the power of establishing, there is the arising of desire, which is the arising of the faculty of mindfulness; through the power of establishing, there is the arising of attention.
The arising of the faculty of mindfulness occurs; through the faculty of mindfulness, the establishment of unity is the arising of the faculty of mindfulness.
For the sake of non-distraction, the arising of adverting is the arising of the faculty of concentration;
through non-distraction, the arising of desire is the arising of the faculty of concentration; through non-distraction, the arising of attention...

The arising of the faculty of concentration is the arising of the faculty of concentration; through the influence of the faculty of concentration, the establishment in unity is the arising of the faculty of concentration.
The arising of the advertence for the purpose of seeing is the arising of the faculty of wisdom; through the mode of seeing, there is the arising of desire.
The arising of the faculty of wisdom occurs through the arising of the faculty of wisdom; the arising of attention by way of seeing is the arising of the faculty of wisdom;
the establishment of unity by way of the faculty of wisdom is the arising of the faculty of wisdom.
The arising of adverting for the purpose of resolution is the arising of the faculty of faith; [the arising of adverting] for the purpose of exertion...
The arising of advertence is the arising of the energy faculty; the arising of advertence in the sense of establishing is the arising of the mindfulness faculty;
the arising of advertence in the sense of non-distraction is the arising of the concentration faculty;
the arising of advertence in the sense of seeing is the arising of the wisdom faculty.
Through the influence of resolve, the arising of desire is the arising of the faculty of faith;

through the influence of exertion, the arising of desire is the arising of the faculty of energy; through the influence of establishment, the arising of desire is the arising of the faculty of mindfulness;
through the influence of non-distraction, the arising of desire is the arising of the faculty of concentration.
There is an arising: through the mode of seeing, the arising of desire is the arising of the faculty of wisdom (*paññindriya*).
Through the mode of resolve, the arising of attention (*manasikāra*) is the arising of the faculty of faith (*saddhindriya*);
through the mode of exertion, the arising of attention is the arising of the faculty of energy (*vīriyindriya*); through the mode of establishment, the arising of attention...
The arising of mindfulness is the arising of the faculty of mindfulness; through non-distraction, the arising of attention is the arising of the faculty of concentration;
through seeing, the arising of attention is the arising of the faculty of wisdom.
Through the influence of the faculty of faith, the establishment of unity is the arising of the faculty of faith; [and] of the faculty of energy...

Through the power of the faculty of energy, the establishment of unity arises as the origination of the faculty of energy; through the power of the faculty of mindfulness, the establishment of unity arises as the origination of the faculty of mindfulness;
through the power of the faculty of concentration, the establishment of unity arises as the origination of the faculty of concentration;
through the power of the faculty of wisdom, the establishment of unity arises as the origination of the faculty of wisdom.
In these forty ways there is the arising of the five faculties; in these forty ways one understands the arising of the five faculties.
In what forty ways is there the passing away of the five faculties;
in what forty ways does one understand the passing away of the five faculties?
With the subsiding of advertence for the sake of resolution, there is the subsiding of the faculty of faith;

with the subsiding of zeal by way of resolution, there is the subsiding of the faculty of faith; with the subsiding of attention by way of resolution, there is the subsiding of the faculty of faith; and through the influence of the faculty of faith, there is the non-appearance of diversity.
There is the subsiding by way of the faculty of faith;
there is the subsiding of the faculty of energy through the subsiding of the adverting [consciousness] whose purpose is exertion,
through the subsiding of desire by way of exertion, and through the subsiding of attention by way of exertion.
The subsiding of the faculty of energy is the subsiding of the faculty of energy; the non-appearance of unity by way of the faculty of energy is the subsiding of the faculty of energy.
The subsiding of adverting for the purpose of establishing mindfulness is the subsiding of the faculty of mindfulness; by way of establishing [mindfulness]...
With the subsiding of desire, there is the subsiding of the faculty of mindfulness;

with the subsiding of attention by way of establishment, there is the subsiding of the faculty of mindfulness; and with the non-establishment of unity by way of the faculty of mindfulness, there is the subsiding of the faculty of mindfulness.
The subsiding of advertence for the sake of non-distraction is the subsiding of the concentration faculty;
through non-distraction, the subsiding of desire is the subsiding of the concentration faculty; through non-distraction, the subsiding of attention is the subsiding of the concentration faculty;
and the non-appearance of diversity by way of the concentration faculty [is also the subsiding of the concentration faculty].
There is the subsiding of the faculty of concentration;
there is the subsiding of the faculty of wisdom through the subsiding of the adverting [of mind] for the purpose of seeing,
and there is the subsiding of the faculty of wisdom through the subsiding of desire by way of seeing, and through the subsiding of attention by way of seeing.
The subsiding of the advertence for the purpose of resolution is the subsiding of the faith faculty; through the faith faculty, the non-appearance of unity is the subsiding of the wisdom faculty.
The subsiding of the advertence for the purpose of exertion... [is the subsiding of the energy faculty].
With the subsiding of adverting for the purpose of exertion, there is the subsiding of the energy faculty;

with the subsiding of adverting for the purpose of establishing, there is the subsiding of the mindfulness faculty; with the subsiding of adverting for the purpose of non-distraction, there is the subsiding of the concentration faculty;
with the subsiding of adverting for the purpose of seeing, there is the subsiding of the wisdom faculty.
Through resolution, the subsiding of desire is the subsiding of the faculty of faith;
through exertion, the subsiding of desire is the subsiding of the faculty of energy; through establishment, the subsiding of desire is the subsiding of the faculty of mindfulness;
through non-distraction, the subsiding of desire is the subsiding of the faculty of concentration.
There is a subsiding; by way of seeing, the subsiding of desire is the subsiding of the faculty of wisdom.
By way of resolution, the subsiding of attention is the subsiding of the faculty of faith.
By way of exertion, the subsiding of attention is the subsiding of the faculty of energy. By way of establishment, the subsiding of attention...
The subsiding of mindfulness is the subsiding of the faculty of mindfulness; through non-distraction, the subsiding of attention is the subsiding of the faculty of concentration;
through seeing, the subsiding of attention is the subsiding of the faculty of wisdom.
Through the influence of the faculty of faith, the non-appearance of unity is the subsiding of the faculty of faith; [through the influence] of the faculty of energy...

Through the power of the faculty of energy, the establishment in unity is the subsiding of the faculty of energy; through the power of the faculty of mindfulness, the establishment in unity is the subsiding of the faculty of mindfulness;
through the power of the faculty of concentration, the establishment in unity is the subsiding of the faculty of concentration;
through the power of the faculty of wisdom, the establishment in unity is the subsiding of the faculty of wisdom.
In these forty ways there is the subsiding of the five faculties; in these forty ways one understands the subsiding of the five faculties.
1.4.2.1. Exposition of Gratification (Assāda-niddesa)
In what twenty-five ways is there gratification in the five faculties? In what twenty-five ways does one understand the gratification in the five faculties?
The non-arising of lack of faith is the gratification of the faculty of faith; the non-arising of the fever of lack of faith...
There is gratification in the faculty of faith; there is confidence in the practice of resolution as gratification in the faculty of faith;
the attainment of peaceful abiding is gratification in the faculty of faith; and whatever pleasure and joy arise dependent upon the faculty of faith—this is the gratification in the faculty of faith.
The non-arising of indolence is the gratification of the faculty of energy; the non-arising of the fever of indolence is the gratification of the faculty of energy;
confidence in the practice of exertion is the gratification of the faculty of energy;
and the attainment of peaceful abiding is the gratification of the faculty of energy—whatever arises dependent upon this faculty of energy.
Pleasure and joy are the gratification of the faculty of energy.
The non-appearance of negligence is the gratification of the faculty of mindfulness; the non-appearance of the fever of negligence is the gratification of the faculty of mindfulness;
confidence in one’s established conduct is the gratification of the faculty of mindfulness.

The attainment of peaceful abiding is the gratification of the faculty of mindfulness; the pleasure and joy that arise dependent upon the faculty of mindfulness—this is the gratification of the faculty of mindfulness.
The non-appearance of restlessness is the gratification of the faculty of concentration; the non-appearance of the fever of restlessness—
There is gratification in the faculty of concentration; there is confidence in the practice of non-distraction as gratification in the faculty of concentration;

the attainment of peaceful abiding is gratification in the faculty of concentration; and whatever pleasure and joy arise dependent upon the faculty of concentration—this is the gratification in the faculty of concentration.
The non-appearance of ignorance is the gratification of the faculty of wisdom; the non-appearance of the fever of ignorance is the gratification of the faculty of wisdom;
confidence in the practice of vision is the gratification of the faculty of wisdom;
the attainment of peaceful abiding is the gratification of the faculty of wisdom—whatever arises dependent upon this faculty of wisdom [is its gratification].
Pleasure and joy: this is the gratification of the faculty of wisdom.
In these twenty-five aspects there is gratification for the five faculties;
in these twenty-five aspects one understands the gratification of the five faculties.
1.4.2.2. Exposition of the Disadvantage (Ādīnavaniddesa) In what twenty-five aspects is there disadvantage in the five faculties?
In what twenty-five aspects does one understand the disadvantage of the five faculties?
The manifestation of lack of faith is a danger to the faculty of faith; the manifestation of the fever of lack of faith is a danger to the faculty of faith;
in the sense of impermanence, there is a danger to the faculty of faith; in the sense of suffering, there is a danger to the faculty of faith;
in the sense of non-self, there is a danger to the faculty of faith.

The manifestation of laziness is a danger to the faculty of energy; the manifestation of the fever of laziness is a danger to the faculty of energy; in the sense of impermanence there is a danger to the faculty of energy; in the sense of suffering … [and so on] … in the sense of non-self there is a danger to the faculty of energy.

The manifestation of negligence is a danger to the faculty of mindfulness; the manifestation of the fever of negligence is a danger to the faculty of mindfulness; in the sense of impermanence there is a danger to the faculty of mindfulness; in the sense of suffering … [and so on] …
In the sense of non-self, there is danger for the faculty of mindfulness.

The manifestation of restlessness is a danger for the faculty of concentration; the manifestation of the fever of restlessness is a danger for the faculty of concentration. In the sense of impermanence, there is danger for the faculty of concentration;
in the sense of suffering …pe… in the sense of non-self, there is danger for the faculty of concentration.
The manifestation of ignorance is a danger to the faculty of wisdom; the manifestation of the fever of ignorance is a danger to the faculty of wisdom;
the aspect of impermanence is a danger to the faculty of wisdom; the aspect of suffering is a danger to the faculty of wisdom;
the aspect of non-self is a danger to the faculty of wisdom.
In these twenty-five ways there is danger in the five faculties;
in these twenty-five ways one understands the danger in the five faculties.
1.4.2.3. Exposition of Escape (Nissaraṇaniddesa)
In what eighty ways is there an escape from the five faculties? In what eighty ways does one understand the escape from the five faculties?
In the sense of resolution, the faculty of faith has escaped from lack of faith; it has escaped from the fever of lack of faith.
It is detached from the defilements that follow after it and from the aggregates; it is detached from all external signs;
and through the acquisition of a faith-faculty more refined than the previous one, it is detached from the former faith-faculty.
In the sense of exertion, the energy-faculty is detached from indolence and detached from the fever of indolence.
It is detached from the defilements and aggregates that follow after it; it is detached from all external signs;
and through the acquisition of a more refined faculty of energy, it is detached from the preceding faculty of energy.
In the sense of establishing, the faculty of mindfulness is detached from negligence, detached from the fever of negligence, and [detached] from the defilements that follow after it.
It is detached from the aggregates; it is detached from all external signs; and by the acquisition of a more refined faculty of mindfulness, it is detached from the preceding faculty of mindfulness.
In the sense of non-distraction, the concentration faculty is detached from restlessness, and it is detached from the fever of restlessness.
It is liberated from the defilements that follow after it and from the aggregates; it is liberated from all external signs;
and through the acquisition of a more refined faculty of concentration, it is liberated from the previously acquired faculty of concentration.
In the sense of seeing, the faculty of wisdom is liberated from ignorance; it is liberated from the fever of ignorance.
It is detached from the defilements and aggregates that follow after it; it is detached from all external signs;
and through the acquisition of a wisdom-faculty more refined than before, it is detached from the previous wisdom-faculty.
In the preliminary stage, by means of the five faculties, the five faculties are detached according to the first jhāna. In the first...
In the first jhāna, by way of the second jhāna, the five faculties are transcended by means of the five faculties;
in the second jhāna, by way of the third jhāna, the five faculties are transcended by means of the five faculties;
in the third jhāna, by way of the fourth jhāna, the five faculties are transcended by means of the five faculties; in the fourth jhāna, by means of the five faculties...
By means of the attainment of the base of infinite space, the five faculties have transcended [the lower realms];
by means of the five faculties in the attainment of the base of infinite space, the five faculties have transcended through the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness;

by means of the five faculties in the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness, the five faculties have transcended through the attainment of the base of nothingness; [and] by means of the attainment of the base of nothingness...
By means of the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception through the five faculties, the five faculties become detached from the five faculties.

By means of the contemplation of impermanence through the five faculties in relation to the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the five faculties become detached from the five faculties;
by means of the contemplation of suffering through the five faculties in relation to the contemplation of impermanence, the five faculties [become detached].
They have escaped: through the five faculties of the contemplation of suffering, the five faculties escape by way of the contemplation of non-self;
through the five faculties of the contemplation of non-self, the five faculties escape by way of the contemplation of disenchantment;
through the five faculties of the contemplation of disenchantment, the five faculties [escape] by way of the contemplation of dispassion.
They have escaped: by means of the five faculties of the contemplation of fading away (*virāga*), the five faculties [of the contemplation of cessation] escape;
by means of the five faculties of the contemplation of cessation, the five faculties escape by way of the contemplation of relinquishment (*paṭinissagga*);
by means of the five faculties of the contemplation of relinquishment, the five faculties escape by way of the contemplation of destruction (*khaya*).
They are detached: through the contemplation of destruction, by way of the contemplation of fall, the five faculties are detached from the five faculties;
through the contemplation of fall, by way of the contemplation of change, the five faculties are detached from the five faculties;
through the contemplation of change, by way of the contemplation of the signless, the five faculties [are detached] from the five faculties.
They have emerged: through the five faculties by way of the contemplation of the signless, the five faculties have emerged through the contemplation of the desireless;
through the five faculties by way of the contemplation of emptiness, the five faculties have emerged through the contemplation of emptiness;
and through the five faculties by way of higher wisdom and insight into phenomena...
The five faculties are transcended.
Through the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena (*adhipaññādhammavipassanā*), by way of knowledge and vision according to reality (*yathābhūtañāṇadassana*), the five faculties are transcended;
and within that knowledge and vision according to reality, by way of contemplation of danger (*ādīnavānupassanā*) through the five faculties, the five faculties are transcended.
They are detached: through the contemplation of danger, by way of the contemplation of reflection, the five faculties are detached from the five faculties;
through the contemplation of reflection, by way of the contemplation of turning away, the five faculties are detached from the five faculties;
through the contemplation of turning away, by way of the stream-entry path, the five faculties are detached from the five faculties.
They exist; by means of the five faculties in the path of stream-entry, the five faculties are transcended through the attainment of the fruit of stream-entry;
by means of the five faculties in the attainment of the fruit of stream-entry, the five faculties are transcended through the path of once-returning;
by means of the five faculties in the path of once-returning, [the five faculties are transcended] through the attainment of the fruit of once-returning.
The five faculties are transcended; by means of the five faculties of the attainment of the fruit of once-returning, the five faculties are transcended through the path of non-returning;
by means of the five faculties of the path of non-returning, the five faculties are transcended through the attainment of the fruit of non-returning;
by means of the five faculties of the attainment of the fruit of non-returning, [the five faculties are transcended] through the path of arahantship.
The five faculties have escaped [from their opposites]. At the path of arahantship, by way of the attainment of the fruit of arahantship through the five faculties, the five faculties have escaped.
In renunciation, the five faculties have escaped from sensual desire; in non-ill will, the five faculties have escaped from ill will.
They have emerged: through the perception of light, the five faculties have emerged from sloth and torpor;
through non-distraction, the five faculties have emerged from restlessness; through the definition of phenomena, the five faculties have emerged from doubt;
through knowledge, the five faculties have emerged from ignorance; through gladness, the five faculties...
They are free from aversion.
In the first jhāna, the five faculties are free from the hindrances;
in the second jhāna, the five faculties are free from applied and sustained thought; in the third jhāna, the five faculties are free from rapture.
In the fourth jhāna, the five faculties are free from pleasure and pain;
in the attainment of the base of infinite space, the five faculties are free from perception of form, perception of resistance, and perception of diversity;
in the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness, the five faculties are free from the perception of the base of infinite space; [and so on] in the attainment of the base of nothingness.
The five faculties have escaped from the perception of the base of infinite consciousness through the base of infinite consciousness;
the five faculties have escaped from the perception of the base of nothingness through the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
Through the contemplation of impermanence, the five faculties have escaped from the perception of permanence; through the contemplation of suffering, the five faculties...

Through the contemplation of suffering, the five faculties become detached from the perception of pleasure; through the contemplation of non-self, the five faculties become detached from the perception of self;
through the contemplation of disenchantment, the five faculties become detached from delight;
through the contemplation of dispassion, the five faculties become detached from lust; and through the contemplation of cessation, the five faculties become detached from origination.
They are escaped: through the contemplation of relinquishment, the five faculties are escaped from grasping;
through the contemplation of destruction, the five faculties are escaped from the perception of compactness; through the contemplation of fall, the five faculties are escaped from accumulation;
through the contemplation of change, the five faculties are escaped from the perception of permanence.
Through the contemplation of the signless, the five faculties are released from signs;
through the contemplation of the desireless, the five faculties are released from desire; through the contemplation of emptiness, the five faculties are released from misapprehension.
Through higher wisdom and insight into phenomena, the five faculties are released from the misapprehension of grasping at a core, in the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are.
Through the contemplation of delusion, the five faculties become free from adherence; through the contemplation of danger, the five faculties become free from adherence to a base;
through the contemplation of reflection, the five faculties become free from non-reflection;
and through the contemplation of turning away, the five faculties become free from adherence to bondage.
On the path of stream-entry, the five faculties are free from the defilements associated with views;
on the path of once-returning, the five faculties are free from gross defilements; on the path of non-returning, the five faculties are free from residual defilements;
and on the path of arahantship, the five faculties are free from all defilements.
For all those whose taints are exhausted, in each respective case, the five faculties have escaped and are well-escaped,
and they are stilled and well-stilled.

1.4.3.3. Exposition of Walking and Dwelling Both his walking and his dwelling are understood and penetrated such that wise fellow-celibates, as he walks and as he dwells, would have confidence in him regarding profound matters, thinking:
"Surely this venerable one has either attained or will attain [the goal]."
"Conduct" (*cariyā*) refers to eight types of conduct:

conduct of postures (*iriyāpatha*), conduct of the sense bases (*āyatana*), conduct of mindfulness (*sati*), conduct of concentration (*samādhi*), conduct of knowledge (*ñāṇa*), conduct of the path (*magga*), conduct of attainment (*patti*), and conduct for the welfare of the world (*lokattha*).
"Conduct of postures" refers to the four postures.
The practice of the sense bases refers to the six internal and external sense bases.
The practice of mindfulness refers to the four foundations of mindfulness.
The practice of concentration refers to the four meditative absorptions.
The conduct of knowledge refers to the four noble truths;
the conduct of the path refers to the four noble paths;
the conduct of attainment refers to the four fruits of recluseship.
"Conduct for the welfare of the world" refers to the Tathāgatas, Arahants, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones; in part, to the Paccekabuddhas; and in part, to the disciples.
It is the conduct of postures for those endowed with aspiration; the conduct of the sense bases for those who guard the doors of the faculties;
the conduct of mindfulness for those dwelling in heedfulness; the conduct of concentration for those devoted to higher consciousness; and the conduct of knowledge.
And there is the conduct of those endowed with wisdom; the conduct on the path of those who have entered the right practice; the conduct of attainment of those who have realized the fruit;

the conduct for the welfare of the world of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones; the conduct of the Paccekabuddhas in part; and the conduct of the disciples in part. These are the eight types of conduct.
There are also eight other modes of conduct:
one who is resolving conducts with faith; one who exerts conducts with energy; one who establishes conducts with mindfulness;
one who brings about non-distraction conducts with concentration; one who understands conducts with wisdom; and one who cognizes conducts with consciousness.
He practices thus: "For one who has practiced in this way, wholesome states flow in," thus he practices the practice of the bases (*āyatanacariyā*);
"One who has practiced in this way attains distinction," thus he practices the practice of distinction (*visesacariyā*)—these are the eight practices.
There are also eight other modes of conduct:
the mode of seeing associated with right view, the mode of directing the mind associated with right intention,
the mode of embracing associated with right speech, the mode of originating associated with right action, and the mode of purification associated with right livelihood.

The practice of exertion is that of right effort; the practice of establishment is that of right mindfulness; and the practice of non-distraction is that of right concentration—these are the eight practices.

As for "dwelling": while resolving, one dwells with faith; while exerting, one dwells with energy; while establishing, one dwells with mindfulness; while effecting non-distraction, one dwells with concentration; and while understanding, one dwells with wisdom.
"Fully understood": the meaning of resolution of the faculty of faith is fully understood; the meaning of exertion of the faculty of energy is fully understood;
the meaning of establishment of the faculty of mindfulness is fully understood; the meaning of non-distraction of the faculty of concentration is fully understood;
the meaning of seeing of the faculty of wisdom is fully understood.
"Penetrated" means that the meaning of resolution of the faith faculty has been penetrated; the meaning of exertion of the energy faculty has been penetrated;
the meaning of establishment of the mindfulness faculty has been penetrated; the meaning of non-distraction of the concentration faculty has been penetrated;
and the meaning of seeing of the wisdom faculty has been penetrated.
"Acting thus" means acting with faith, acting with energy, acting with mindfulness, acting with concentration, and acting with wisdom.
"Dwelling thus" means dwelling with faith, dwelling with energy, dwelling with mindfulness, dwelling with concentration, and dwelling with wisdom.
"The wise one" refers to one who is discerning, insightful, intelligent, learned, and endowed with understanding.
“Fellow-practitioners of the holy life” means those who share the same formal acts, the same recitations, and the same training.

“In profound matters” refers to what are called profound matters: the meditative absorptions (*jhāna*), the liberations (*vimokkha*), the concentrations (*samādhi*), the attainments (*samāpatti*), the paths (*magga*), the fruits (*phala*), the direct knowledges (*abhiññā*), and the analytical insights (*paṭisambhidā*).
“They would have confidence” means they would believe and be resolved in them.
“Addhā” is a term of certainty, a term free from doubt, a term free from uncertainty, a term without duality, a term without ambiguity, a term of necessity,
a term that is categorical, a term of establishment— it is “addhā. “Āyasmā” is a term of endearment, a term of respect, a designation for one who possesses reverence and deference.
"Venerable sir":
"attained" means reached;
"will attain" means will reach.
The third exposition of the suttas is concluded.

this is the initial purification of the faculty of energy.

1.4.4.3. Exposition of the Sense of Predominance How are the faculties to be regarded in the sense of predominance?
A desire arises for the cultivation of the faculty of faith.
Through the influence of desire and through the influence of faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Through the influence of desire, gladness arises;
through the influence of gladness and through the influence of faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Through the influence of gladness, rapture arises;
through the influence of rapture and the influence of faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Through the influence of rapture, tranquility arises.
Through the influence of tranquility and through the influence of faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Through the influence of tranquility, happiness arises;
through the influence of that happiness and through the influence of faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Through happiness, illumination arises;
through illumination, faith arises; through faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Through illumination, a sense of spiritual urgency arises.
Through the influence of spiritual urgency and through the influence of faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Having stirred the mind with urgency, one concentrates it—
through the influence of concentration and through the influence of faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
He firmly exerts the mind thus concentrated;
through that exertion and through faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
He closely looks on with equanimity at the mind thus exerted.
By way of equanimity and by way of faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
By way of equanimity, the mind is liberated from various defilements;
by way of liberation and by way of faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Because they are liberated, those states become of a single flavor;
in the sense of having a single flavor, through the process of development and by means of faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Because it has been developed, they emerge from that toward what is more refined.
By way of turning away, through faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Because of having turned away, one relinquishes;
through relinquishment, through faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
Because they have been relinquished, they cease from that point;
by way of cessation, through the influence of faith, the faculty of faith becomes predominant.
By way of cessation, there are two kinds of relinquishment.
There is the relinquishment of renunciation and the relinquishment of leaping forward.
One renounces both defilements and aggregates;
thus, it is the relinquishment of renunciation.
"The mind leaps forward into the element of cessation-nirvana"—
this is leaping-forward relinquishment.
By way of cessation, these are the two kinds of relinquishment.
Zeal arises for the abandoning of lack of faith … zeal arises for the abandoning of the fever of lack of faith … zeal arises for the abandoning of those defilements associated with views …
Zeal arises for the abandoning of gross defilements… zeal arises for the abandoning of residual defilements… zeal arises for the abandoning of all defilements.
Through the influence of desire and through the influence of faith,
the faculty of faith becomes predominant … [and so on] … desire arises for the development of the faculty of energy … desire arises for the abandoning of sloth.
Zeal arises for the abandoning of the fever of laziness;
zeal arises for the abandoning of the defilements that act as fetters through views; ... pe ...
zeal arises for the abandoning of all defilements.
Zeal arises for the development of the faculty of mindfulness … [and so on] … zeal arises for the abandoning of negligence … zeal arises for the abandoning of the fever of negligence … [and so on].
Zeal arises for the abandoning of all defilements;
zeal arises for the development of the faculty of concentration...
[and so on] ...zeal arises for the abandoning of restlessness; zeal arises for the abandoning of the fever of restlessness... [and so on].
Zeal arises for the abandoning of all defilements;
zeal arises for the development of the faculty of wisdom; ... pe ...
zeal arises for the abandoning of ignorance.
Zeal arises for the abandoning of the fever of ignorance… zeal arises for the abandoning of the defilements associated with views… zeal arises for the abandoning of gross defilements…
Zeal arises for the abandoning of the defilements associated with the subtle (anusahagata);
zeal arises for the abandoning of all defilements.
Through the influence of zeal and through the influence of wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Through the influence of joy, gladness arises;
through the influence of gladness, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant by way of wisdom.
Through the influence of gladness, rapture arises.
Through the influence of rapture, through the influence of wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Through the influence of rapture, tranquility arises;
through the influence of that tranquility and the influence of wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Through tranquility, happiness arises;
through happiness and wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Through happiness, illumination arises.
Through the influence of illumination and through the influence of wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Through the influence of illumination, a sense of spiritual urgency arises;
through that sense of urgency and through the influence of wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Having stirred the mind, he concentrates it;
through the power of concentration and the power of wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
He firmly exerts that well-concentrated mind.
By way of exertion and by way of wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
He carefully looks on with equanimity at the mind thus exerted—
by way of equanimity and by way of wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
By means of equanimity, the mind is liberated from various defilements;
through liberation, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant by way of wisdom.
Because they are liberated, those states become of a single flavor.
Through the influence of development and through the influence of wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Because they have been developed, they turn away from what is even more refined than that—
through the influence of turning away and through the influence of wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Because of its turning away, one relinquishes from there;
by way of relinquishment and by way of wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Because of having relinquished, they cease from there.
Through cessation and through wisdom, the faculty of wisdom becomes predominant.
Through cessation there are two kinds of relinquishment:
relinquishment by giving up and relinquishment by leaping forward.
He relinquishes both defilements and aggregates; thus it is the renunciation of relinquishing.
The mind leaps forward into the element of nibbāna, which is cessation; thus it is...
The leap and the relinquishment.
These two relinquishments are by way of cessation.
Thus, the faculties are to be regarded in the sense of preponderance.
The Second Recitation Section.
1.4.4.4. Exposition of the Meaning of Resolution.
How are the faculties (indriya) to be regarded in the sense of resolution?
Zeal arises for the development of the faculty of faith;
through zeal and through faith, one resolves upon the faculty of faith.
Through zeal, gladness arises.
By means of gladness and by means of faith, one resolves upon the faculty of faith … [and so on] … Thus, the faculties are to be seen in the sense of resolution.
1.4.4.5. Exposition of the Sense of Exhaustion.
How are the faculties to be regarded in the sense of exhaustion?
In the sense of resolution, the faculty of faith exhausts lack of faith and exhausts the fever of lack of faith.
In the sense of exertion, the faculty of energy exhausts laziness and exhausts the fever of laziness.
In the sense of establishing, the faculty of mindfulness consumes negligence and consumes the fever of negligence.
In the sense of non-distraction, the faculty of concentration consumes restlessness and consumes the fever of restlessness.
In the sense of seeing, the faculty of wisdom consumes ignorance and consumes the fever of ignorance.
In renunciation, the five faculties overcome sensual desire.
In non-ill will, the five faculties overcome ill will.
In the perception of light, the five faculties overcome sloth and torpor.
In non-distraction, the five faculties overcome restlessness …pe… in the path of arahantship, the five faculties overcome all defilements.
Thus, the faculties are to be regarded in the sense of overcoming.
1.4.4.6. Exposition of the Meaning of Establishing In what sense are the faculties to be regarded as "establishing"?
The faculty of faith establishes itself in resolution; it establishes the faculty of faith in one who possesses faith in resolution.
One who possesses energy establishes the faculty of energy in exertion; one who possesses energy establishes the faculty of energy in exertion for another.
One who possesses mindfulness establishes the faculty of mindfulness in establishment; one who possesses mindfulness establishes the faculty of mindfulness in establishment for another.
One who is concentrated establishes the faculty of concentration in non-distraction; one who is concentrated establishes the faculty of concentration in non-distraction for another.
The wise person establishes the faculty of wisdom in vision; the faculty of wisdom of the wise person is established in vision.
The practitioner establishes the five faculties in renunciation; the five faculties of the practitioner are established in renunciation.
The practitioner establishes the five faculties in non-ill will; the five faculties of the practitioner are established in non-ill will.
The practitioner establishes the five faculties in the perception of light; the five faculties establish the practitioner in the perception of light.

The practitioner establishes the five faculties in non-distraction; the five faculties establish the practitioner in non-distraction …pe… the practitioner establishes the five faculties in the path of arahantship; the five faculties establish the practitioner in the path of arahantship.
Thus should the faculties be regarded in the sense of being established.
This concludes the fourth exposition of the Suttanta.
1.4.5. The Coordination of the Faculties.
In how many ways is an ordinary person skilled in the manifestation when developing concentration?
In how many ways is one in training skilled in the manifestation when developing concentration?
In how many ways is one free from lust skilled in the manifestation when developing concentration?
When an ordinary person develops concentration, they are skilled in its establishment in seven ways.
When one in training develops concentration, they are skilled in its establishment in eight ways.
When one free from lust develops concentration, they are skilled in its establishment in ten ways.
When an ordinary person develops concentration, in what seven ways is he skilled in its manifestation?

Through the fact of having adverted, he is skilled in the manifestation of the object; he is skilled in the manifestation of the sign of serenity; he is skilled in the manifestation of the sign of exertion;
he is skilled in the manifestation of non-distraction; he is skilled in the manifestation of light; he is skilled in the manifestation of encouragement.
He is skilled in the appearance of equanimity.
When an ordinary person develops concentration, he is skilled in its appearance in these seven ways.
When a trainee develops concentration, in what eight ways is he skilled in its appearance?
Because of having directed his mind, he is skilled in the appearance of the object, skilled in the appearance of the sign of serenity, skilled in the appearance of the sign of exertion,
skilled in the appearance of non-distraction, skilled in the appearance of light, skilled in the appearance of encouragement,
skilled in the appearance of equanimity, and skilled in the appearance of unity.
A trainee developing concentration is skilled in establishing it in these eight ways.
When one free from lust develops concentration, in what ten ways is he skilled in establishing it?

Through having adverted, he is skilled in the establishment of the object; ... [as before] ... he is skilled in the establishment of unity, skilled in the establishment of knowledge, and skilled in the establishment of liberation.
One who is free from lust, while developing concentration, is skilled in establishing [the mind] in these ten aspects.
When an ordinary person develops insight, in how many aspects is he skilled in establishing, and in how many aspects is he unskilled in establishing?
When one in training develops insight, in how many aspects is he skilled in establishing, and in how many aspects is he unskilled in establishing?
When one who is free from lust develops insight, in how many ways is he skilled in manifestation, and in how many ways is he skilled in non-manifestation?
When an ordinary person develops insight, he is skilled in manifestation in nine ways and skilled in non-manifestation in nine ways.
When a trainee develops insight, he is skilled in manifestation in ten ways and skilled in non-manifestation in ten ways.
One who is free from lust, when developing insight, is skilled in appearance in twelve ways and skilled in non-appearance in twelve ways.
When an ordinary person develops insight, in which nine ways is he skilled in appearance, and in which nine ways is he skilled in non-appearance?
He is skilled in appearance as impermanent and skilled in non-appearance as permanent.
He is skilled in the appearance of things as suffering, and skilled in the non-appearance of them as pleasure.
He is skilled in the appearance of things as non-self, and skilled in the non-appearance of them as self.
He is skilled in the appearance of things as subject to destruction, and skilled in the non-appearance of them as solid.

He is skilled in the appearance of impermanence, and skilled in the non-appearance of permanence. He is skilled in the appearance of suffering, and skilled in the non-appearance of pleasure. He is skilled in the appearance of non-self, and skilled in the non-appearance of self.

He is skilled in the appearance of the conditioned, and skilled in the non-appearance of the unconditioned. He is skilled in the appearance of the formed, and skilled in the non-appearance of the formless. He is skilled in the appearance of the determinate, and skilled in the non-appearance of the indeterminate. He is skilled in the appearance of the compounded, and skilled in the non-appearance of the uncompounded. He is skilled in the appearance of the arisen, and skilled in the non-appearance of the unarisen. He is skilled in the appearance of the originated, and skilled in the non-appearance of the unoriginated. He is skilled in the appearance of the dependently arisen, and skilled in the non-appearance of the non-dependently arisen. He is skilled in the appearance of the passing away, and skilled in the non-appearance of the non-passing-away. He is skilled in the appearance of the accumulation, and skilled in the non-appearance of the non-accumulation. He is skilled in the appearance of change, and skilled in the non-appearance of stability. He is skilled in the appearance of the signless, and skilled in the non-appearance of signs.
He is skilled in the appearance of the wishless and skilled in the non-appearance of wishing.
He is skilled in the appearance of emptiness and skilled in the non-appearance of misinterpretation.
When a worldling develops insight, he is skilled in these nine modes of appearance and skilled in these nine modes of non-appearance.
When a trainee develops insight, in what ten aspects is he skilled in its manifestation, and in what ten aspects is he skilled in its non-manifestation?

He is skilled in its manifestation as impermanent, and skilled in its non-manifestation as permanent … [and so on] … he is skilled in its manifestation as empty, and skilled in its non-manifestation as misapprehension.
He is skilled in its manifestation as knowledge, and skilled in its non-manifestation as ignorance.
A trainee developing insight is skilled in appearance in these ten aspects, and skilled in non-appearance in these ten aspects.
One free from lust developing insight: in which twelve aspects is he skilled in appearance, and in which twelve aspects is he skilled in non-appearance?
He is skilled in appearance as impermanent, and skilled in non-appearance as permanent … [and so on] … he is skilled in appearance as knowledge, and skilled in non-appearance as ignorance.
He is skilled in the appearance of disjunction and skilled in the non-appearance of conjunction.
He is skilled in the appearance of cessation and skilled in the non-appearance of formations.
When one who is free from lust develops insight, he is skilled in appearance in these twelve ways and skilled in non-appearance in these twelve ways.

Because of having adverted [to the object], by way of skill in the manifestation of the object, he coordinates the faculties (*indriya*), understands their range (*gocara*), and penetrates their capacity.
…pe… He coordinates the states (*dhamma*), understands their range, and penetrates their capacity.
How does he coordinate the faculties? How does he coordinate the faculties?
He coordinates the faculty of faith in the sense of resolution … [and so on] … by way of skill in the appearance of the sign of serenity,
by way of skill in the appearance of the sign of exertion, by way of skill in the appearance of non-distraction, by way of skill in the appearance of illumination,
by way of skill in the appearance of encouragement, by way of skill in the appearance of equanimity, and by way of skill in the appearance of unity.
By way of skill in the manifestation of knowledge, and by way of skill in the manifestation of liberation.
By way of skill in the manifestation [of things] as impermanent, and by way of skill in the non-manifestation [of them] as permanent;

by way of skill in the manifestation [of things] as suffering, and by way of skill in the non-manifestation [of them] as pleasure; by way of skill in the manifestation [of things] as non-self, and by way of skill in the non-manifestation [of them] as self.
By way of skill in the appearance of passing away; by way of skill in the non-appearance of compactness; by way of skill in the appearance of vanishing;
by way of skill in the non-appearance of accumulation; by way of skill in the appearance of change; by way of skill in the non-appearance of permanence;
by way of skill in the appearance of the signless; by way of skill in the non-appearance of signs; and by way of skill in the appearance of the desireless.
By way of skill in the non-appearance of aspiration, skill in the appearance of emptiness, skill in the non-appearance of misapprehension,
skill in the appearance of knowledge, skill in the non-appearance of ignorance, skill in the appearance of disengagement,
skill in the non-appearance of bondage, skill in the appearance of cessation, and skill in the non-appearance of formations.
One coordinates the faculties, understands their range, and penetrates their capacity.
Wisdom that consists in mastery over three faculties in sixty-four modes is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints.
Which three faculties?
The faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*), and the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*).
To how many bases does the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" go?
To how many bases does the faculty of final knowledge go?
To how many bases does the faculty of one who has already known go?
The faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" goes to one base:
the path of stream-entry.
The faculty of final knowledge proceeds to six states:
the fruit of stream-entry, the path of once-returning, the fruit of once-returning, the path of non-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the path of arahantship.
The faculty of one who has already known proceeds to one state: [the fruit of arahantship].
The fruit of arahantship.
At the moment of the stream-entry path, the faculty of faith has resolution as its accompaniment;
the faculty of energy has exertion as its accompaniment; the faculty of mindfulness has establishment as its accompaniment; the faculty of concentration...
The faculty of non-distraction has concentration as its retinue; the faculty of wisdom has vision as its retinue; the faculty of mind has cognition as its retinue;
the faculty of mental pleasure has suffusion as its retinue; the life-faculty has the predominance of the continuity of occurrence as its retinue.
At the moment of the stream-entry path, all states that have arisen—excluding mind-originated matter—are wholesome.
All are free from taints, all lead out, all conduce to dispersal,
all are supramundane, and all have Nibbāna as their object.
At the moment of the path of stream-entry, these eight faculties are the companions and attendants of the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown."
They are mutual attendants, they are attendants by way of support, they are attendants by way of association,
they are co-existent, they are conascent, they are conjoined, and they are associated.
These very factors are both its modes and its attendants.
At the moment of the fruit of stream-entry …pe… at the moment of the fruit of arhatship,
the faculty of faith is accompanied by the resolve of the faculty of final knowledge;
…pe… the life-faculty is accompanied by the predominance of the continuity of the process [of existence].

At the moment of the fruit of arahantship, all phenomena that have arisen are indeterminate (*abyākata*); with the exception of mind-originated matter, all are free from taints (*anāsava*), all are supramundane (*lokuttara*), and all have Nibbāna as their object.
At the moment of the fruit of arahantship, these eight faculties are the co-nascent attendants of the faculty of one who has known (*aññātāvindriya*).
They are both its modes and its attendants.
Thus, these eight groups of eight make sixty-four.
Regarding "taints" (āsavā): what are those taints?
They are the taint of sensual desire (kāmāsava), the taint of existence (bhavāsava), the taint of views (diṭṭhāsava), and the taint of ignorance (avijjāsava).
Where do these taints (āsava) come to exhaustion?
By the path of stream-entry (sotāpatti-magga), the taint of views (diṭṭhāsava) is exhausted without remainder.

The taint of sensual desire (kāmāsava) leading to states of deprivation is exhausted; the taint of existence (bhavāsava) leading to states of deprivation is exhausted; and the taint of ignorance (avijjāsava) leading to states of deprivation is exhausted.
It is here that these taints are exhausted.
By means of the path of the once-returner, the gross taint of sensual desire is exhausted; the corresponding taint of existence is exhausted; the corresponding taint of ignorance is exhausted.
It is here that these taints are exhausted.

By the path of non-returning, the taint of sensual desire is exhausted without remainder; the taint of existence associated with it is exhausted; and the taint of ignorance associated with it is exhausted.
It is here that these taints are exhausted.
By the path of arahantship, the taint of existence is exhausted without remainder, and the taint of ignorance is exhausted without remainder.
Here these taints are exhausted.
For him, there is nothing more to be seen here,
nor anything further to be known or understood.
"He has directly known everything that is to be known;
therefore the Tathāgata is 'All-Seeing' (Samantacakkhu).
In what sense is he "All-Seeing"? In the sense of having eyes everywhere.
The fourteen knowledges of a Buddha:
knowledge of suffering is a Buddha-knowledge; knowledge of the origin of suffering is a Buddha-knowledge …pe… omniscience is a Buddha-knowledge;
unobstructed knowledge is a Buddha-knowledge.
These are the fourteen kinds of Buddha-knowledge.
Of these fourteen kinds of Buddha-knowledge, eight are shared with disciples, while six are not shared with disciples.
To the extent that the meaning of suffering as suffering is known, there is no meaning of suffering unknown.
The universal eye.
That which is the universal eye is the faculty of wisdom (*paññindriya*).

By way of the faculty of wisdom, there is the faculty of faith in the sense of resolution; the faculty of energy in the sense of exertion; the faculty of mindfulness in the sense of establishment; and the faculty of concentration in the sense of non-distraction.
To the extent that the meaning of suffering as suffering has been seen, known, realized, and touched with wisdom—
there being no meaning of suffering untouched by wisdom—
this is the universal eye.
That which is the universal eye is the faculty of wisdom (*paññindriya*).

By way of the faculty of wisdom, there is the faculty of faith (*saddhindriya*) in the sense of resolution; the faculty of energy (*vīriyindriya*) in the sense of exertion; the faculty of mindfulness (*satindriya*) in the sense of establishment; and the faculty of concentration (*samādhindriya*) in the sense of non-distraction.
To whatever extent there is the sense of origination regarding origination … [and so forth] …

To the extent that there is the meaning of cessation in cessation … to the extent that there is the meaning of the path in the path … to the extent that there is the meaning of the analytical knowledge of meaning in the analytical knowledge of meaning …
To the extent that there is the meaning of the analytical knowledge of phenomena (dhamma-paṭisambhidā),
to the extent that there is the meaning of the analytical knowledge of linguistic expression (nirutti-paṭisambhidā),
and to the extent that there is the meaning of the analytical knowledge of eloquence (paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā)...
To the extent of the knowledge of the higher and lower faculties of beings;
to the extent of the knowledge of the inclinations and latent tendencies of beings;
to the extent of the knowledge of the Twin Miracle.
To the extent that there is knowledge of the attainment of great compassion...

to the extent that there is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, reached, sought after, and investigated by mind in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans— that has been known and seen.
It is known, realized, and touched by wisdom.
Because there is nothing untouched by wisdom,
he is called the All-Seeing One.
That which is the all-seeing eye is the faculty of wisdom (*paññindriya*).

By way of the faculty of wisdom, there is the faculty of faith (*saddhindriya*) in the sense of resolution; the faculty of energy (*vīriyindriya*) in the sense of exertion; the faculty of mindfulness (*satindriya*) in the sense of establishment; and the faculty of concentration (*samādhindriya*) in the sense of non-distraction.
One who has faith exerts; one who exerts has faith.
While having faith, one establishes [the mind]; while establishing [the mind], one has faith.
While having faith, one concentrates; while concentrating, one has faith.
While having faith, one understands; while understanding, one has faith.
While exerting, one establishes; while establishing, one exerts.
While exerting, one concentrates; while concentrating, one exerts.
While exerting, one understands; while understanding, one exerts.
While exerting, one has faith; while having faith, one exerts.
While establishing, one concentrates; while concentrating, one establishes.
While establishing, one understands; while understanding, one establishes.
While establishing, one has faith; while having faith, one establishes.
While exerting, one grasps; while grasping, one establishes.
While concentrating, one understands; while understanding, one concentrates.
While concentrating, one has faith; while having faith, one concentrates.
While concentrating, one exerts; while exerting, one concentrates.
While concentrating, one establishes [mindfulness]; while establishing, one concentrates.
One who understands has faith; one who has faith understands.
One who understands exerts; one who exerts understands.
One who understands establishes [mindfulness]; one who establishes [mindfulness] understands.
Understanding, one concentrates; concentrating, one understands.
Because of faith, there is exertion; because of exertion, there is faith.
Because of faith, there is establishment; because of establishment, there is faith.
Because it is believed in, it is concentrated; because it is concentrated, it is believed in.
Because it is believed in, it is understood; because it is understood, it is believed in.
Because it is exerted, it is established; because it is established, it is exerted.
Because it is exerted, it is concentrated; because it is concentrated, it is exerted.
Because it is exerted, it is understood; because it is understood, it is exerted.
Because it is exerted, it is believed in; because it is believed in, it is exerted.
Because it is established, it is concentrated; because it is concentrated, it is established.
Because it is established, it is understood; because it is understood, it is established.
Because it is established, it is believed in; because it is believed in, it is established.
Because it is established, it is exerted; because it is exerted, it is established.
Because it is concentrated, it is understood; because it is understood, it is concentrated.
Because it is concentrated, it is believed in; because it is believed in, it is concentrated.
Because it is concentrated, it is exerted; because it is exerted, it is concentrated.
Because it is concentrated, it is established; because it is established, it is concentrated.
Because it is understood, it is believed; because it is believed, it is understood.
Because it is understood, it is exerted; because it is exerted, it is understood.
Because it is understood, it is established; because it is established, it is understood.
Because it is understood, it is concentrated; because it is concentrated, it is understood.

That which is the Buddha-eye is the Buddha-knowledge; that which is the Buddha-knowledge is the Buddha-eye. By means of this eye, the Tathāgata sees beings—those with little dust and those with much dust, those with sharp faculties and those with dull faculties, those of good disposition and those of bad disposition, those easy to instruct and those difficult to instruct—and some who see the danger of blame and the fear of the next world, while others do not.
They do not see the fear of wrongdoing regarding the world beyond.
A person with little dust in their eyes is one who has faith; a person with much dust in their eyes is one who lacks faith.
A person who has aroused energy has little dust in their eyes; a person who is lazy has much dust in their eyes.
A person who is established in mindfulness has little dust on their eyes; a person who is muddled in mindfulness has much dust on their eyes.
A person who is concentrated has little dust on their eyes; a person who is unconcentrated has much dust on their eyes.
A person who is wise has little dust on their eyes; a person who is unwise has much dust on their eyes.
Regarding "sharp-facultied" and "dull-facultied": a person with faith has sharp faculties; a person without faith has dull faculties...
[and so on] ...a person with wisdom has sharp faculties; a person of poor wisdom has dull faculties.
Regarding "of good appearance" and "of bad appearance": a person with faith is of good appearance; a person without faith is of bad appearance... [and so on] ...
A person possessing wisdom is easy to instruct; a person lacking wisdom is difficult to instruct.
Regarding "easy to instruct" and "difficult to instruct": a person endowed with faith is easy to instruct; a person devoid of faith is difficult to instruct ...
[and so on] ... a person possessing wisdom is easy to instruct; a person lacking wisdom is difficult to instruct.

"Some see fear in the other world and in wrongdoing, while others do not see fear in the other world and in wrongdoing. Herein, a person endowed with faith sees fear in the other world and in wrongdoing;

a person lacking faith does not see fear in the other world and in wrongdoing. A person who has aroused energy sees fear in the other world and in wrongdoing; a person who is lazy does not see fear in the other world and in wrongdoing...
[and so on] ...a person possessed of wisdom sees fear in the other world and in wrongdoing; a person of poor wisdom does not see fear in the other world and in wrongdoing.
"World" means the world of aggregates, the world of elements, the world of sense bases, the world of misfortune and its origin, and the world of prosperity and its origin.
There is one world:
all beings subsist by nutriment.
Two worlds:
name and form. Three worlds: [name, form, and consciousness].
The three feelings.
The four worlds—
the four nutriments.
Five worlds—
the five aggregates of clinging.
Six worlds—
There are six internal sense bases.
There are seven worlds—
the seven stations of consciousness.
Eight worlds—
the eight worldly conditions.
Nine worlds—
The nine abodes of beings.
The ten worlds—
the ten bases.
Twelve worlds—
the twelve sense bases.
Eighteen worlds—
The eighteen elements.
All defilements are blameworthy; all misconduct is blameworthy; all volitional formations are blameworthy; all kamma leading to existence is blameworthy.
Thus, in this world and regarding this blame, an intense perception of danger becomes established, just as one would have toward an executioner with a raised sword.
In these fifty ways, one knows, sees, understands, and penetrates these five faculties.
This concludes the third section for recitation.
The Discourse on the Faculties is finished.
